newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU poised to agree key EMU preparations - Santer.
newsitem.headline: EU poised to agree key EMU preparations - Santer.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer expects the European Union to agree crucial preparations for a single currency by mid-December, according to a speech read on his behalf on Monday.

The speech said Santer expected agreement on an EU budget stability pact to be reached by the Dublin EU summit on December 13 and 14. A successor to the current Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) was also expected to be agreed at the summit, it said.
Santer was due to read his speech as the keynote address at the European Finance Convention in Dublin, but could not travel to Dublin because of ill health, organisers said.
His speech was read on his behalf by Colm Larkin, director of the commission representation in Ireland.
"I expect that by the European Council in Dublin there will be agreement on the outstanding issues concerning the stability pact," Santer's speech said.

The stability pact is a mechanism designed to ensure fiscal discipline among countries that join a single currency, by warning countries which step out of line and fining them if they do not improve their public finances.
"I am convinced that, at the European Council in Dublin, there will also be agreement on the new exchange rate mechanism based on strengthened convergence," the speech said.
The new exchange rate mechanism, or ERM2, would link the single currency, the euro, with EU currencies which remain outside it.
Santer's speech said the last of the technical preparations for a single currency -- the establishment of a legal framework to govern it -- would also be "broadly agreed" in Dublin.
The speech said Santer was convinced that Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) would proceed on schedule in 1999.

"It is now possible to state with the greatest degree of confidence that the project has become irreversible and that the euro will see the light of day on January 1, 1999," it said. "Therefore I cannot accept those voices calling for a delay."
The speech attacked the claims of EMU's opponents. "Each time, new stories are invented why the euro would be a disaster," it said. "I am highly amazed by such stories."
The momentum of the single currency drive would increase as 1999 approached, Santer's speech said.

"We have a little more than two years to go," it said. "Two years in which the preparations will intensify, investments will be made and the awareness about the euro will increase. Everybody should prepare for the departure of the Euro train."
